Title: Kenanga raises KJTS earnings forecasts on new Thailand cooling contracts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KJTS Group Bhd's latest cooling contracts in Thailand have prompted Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd (Kenanga IB) to raise its earnings forecasts for the company, citing stronger recurring income from the 20-year agreements.
Kenanga IB raised its financial year 2026 (FY26) and FY27 earnings forecasts for KJTS by two per cent and five per cent, respectively, after factoring in four new projects secured by its Thailand unit, KJTN Engineering Co Ltd.
It also raised its target price to RM1.60 from RM1.57 while maintaining its "Outperform" call on the stock.
KJTN Engineering had entered into four 20-year agreements with wholly owned subsidiaries of Central Plaza Hotel Public Company Ltd (Centel) to undertake cooling system retrofit works, as well as provide operation and maintenance (O&M) services and chilled water supply to four hotels in Thailand.
The hotels are Centara Reserve Samui, Centara Hotel Hat Yai, Centara Grand Beach Resort Phuket and Centara Karon Resort Phuket.
Kenanga IB analyst Tan Sue Wen said the projects involved total retrofit expenditure of about RM11 million, which would ultimately be funded by KJTS, while the O&M and chilled water supply services would run from March 2027 to February 2047.
The agreements carry fixed fees of about RM48 million over 20 years, equivalent to RM2.4 million in annual recurring revenue, excluding variable fees linked to chilled water consumption.
"We are positive on the agreements, as they further strengthen KJTS's recurring income base with a 20-year tenure, while expanding its energy services footprint in Thailand," Tan said.
Kenanga IB estimated that the projects could generate a high-single-digit internal rate of return, assuming an 80:20 debt-to-equity funding structure.
The firm said KJTS had a relatively low gross gearing ratio of 0.23 times as at June 30, 2026, and did not foresee major hurdles in securing financing for the projects.
The retrofit works are expected to start this month and be completed by February 2027, after which the 20-year O&M and chilled water supply period will begin.
KJTS will also receive monthly variable fees based on the amount of chilled water supplied, providing additional revenue beyond the fixed fees.
Kenanga IB said Thailand remained a key growth market for KJTS, with rising adoption of energy efficiency and decarbonisation initiatives across commercial buildings expected to support demand for cooling optimisation and energy management solutions.
"Given that air-conditioning is typically one of the largest sources of electricity consumption in commercial properties, we believe KJTS remains well positioned to capture further opportunities as building owners seek to lower energy costs and improve operating efficiency," it added.
Separately, CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd analyst Walter Aw Lik Hsin said the fixed monthly fees across the four projects amounted to about RM47.8 million over the 20-year tenure.
"We estimate the variable component could reach up to about 50 per cent of the fixed charges, implying potential total fees of up to around RM71.7 million over 20 years, versus RM47.8 million from the fixed component alone," he said.
Aw maintained his "Buy" call on KJTS and a target price of RM1.35.
He said the latest wins represented another milestone for KJTS's Thailand operations, while continued project awards from Central Group strengthened its track record with the existing customer.
KJTN Engineering had previously undertaken three cooling projects for Central Group, which could pave the way for further opportunities across the conglomerate's property portfolio.
KJTS said the latest agreements were expected to contribute positively to the group's earnings and net assets over the contract period.
The company is also required to fund part of the retrofit works through internally generated funds or bank borrowings.
The latest contracts strengthen KJTS's strategy of building a regional energy services business supported by long-term customer relationships and recurring revenue streams.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kerjaya Prospek lands maiden data centre job worth RM858mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd's unit Kerjaya Prospek (M) Sdn Bhd has secured an RM858 million contract for fit-out works at a data centre in Johor.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the contract involves the execution and completion of mechanical, electrical and plumbing fit-out works for the project, which is expected to commence in the third quarter.
The project is targeted for completion within eight months.
Kerjaya chief executive officer and executive director Tee Eng Tiong said the award marked an important milestone for the company in the data centre sector.
"We view this project as a strong starting point to establish our presence in the data centre space.
"Beyond the immediate contribution to our order book, the project will further enhance our capabilities, execution track record and industry expertise, positioning us to pursue a broader range of opportunities within this high-growth sector," he said.
The latest win brings the group's total new contract wins for 2026 to RM3.2 billion, further strengthening its earnings visibility and construction pipeline.
"Meanwhile, our outstanding order book has reached a record RM5.9 billion, providing a strong foundation for sustained revenue contribution over the coming years," Tee said.
At the midday break, Kerjaya Prospek's share price rose 3.12 per cent, or nine sen, to RM2.97, valuing the company at RM3.76 billion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kedah Umno hits back at MoF over KKDW delayed contractor payments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kedah Umno has questioned the Finance Ministry's (MoF) response to Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's remarks on delays in payments to contractors.
Kedah Umno information chief Datuk Shaiful Hazizy Zainol Abidin said it is inappropriate for a senior official to publicly respond to the deputy prime minister in such a manner.
"Kedah Umno takes the statement by the Treasury secretary-general who claimed that the rural and regional development ministry had spent beyond its allocation seriously.
"Any explanation on the matter should have come from the finance minister or deputy finance minister," he said in a statement today.
Shaiful said the claims also raised concerns, as the government's financial system did not allow ministries to spend as they pleased.
He said every project was subject to approval, specific allocation details and financial controls through the Integrated Government Financial Management and Accounting System.
"MoF cannot simply compare annual allocations with total expenditure without taking into account contractual commitments dating back to 2019 to 2021.
"Letters of acceptance were issued before the pandemic, while payment claims were carried forward to subsequent years when the projects resumed," he said.
Shaiful said once work had been completed, the government was responsible for paying contractors based on work progress and its contractual obligations.
He said these earlier commitments could not simply be portrayed as the rural and regional development ministry having "overspent."
"MoF's explanation regarding the RM300 million is also misleading.
"The amount was not a new additional allocation but was channelled through a warrant of authority to spend on the afternoon of Sept 1, after the deputy prime minister raised the issue of delayed payments that same morning," he said.
He also said the allocation was not paid directly by the ministry to contractors but was channelled through the Public Works Department or agencies overseeing the projects.
"As such, the entire approval and payment chain needs to be explained," he said.
Shaiful Hazizy also questioned as to why the ministry should be solely blamed for outstanding payments if the projects had been approved, SSTs issued and work carried out.
"MoF needs to come forward with a breakdown of warrants, contractual commitments and actual disbursement records.
"It should not hide behind broad figures to cover up its own delays and shift the blame onto rural ministry," he said.
Yesterday, MoF
refuted claims
of budget cuts or restrictions on the rural and regional development ministry's allocation for rural road projects, clarifying that all approved funds have been fully channelled.
Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said recent payment delays to contractors stem from the ministry exhausting nearly its entire current-year allocation due to years of overspending beyond its approved parliamentary budgets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Students go behind the scenes of news operations at Media Prima
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: About 20 students from Kolej Profesional Mara Seri Iskandar (KPMSI) today gained first-hand exposure to newsroom and broadcasting operations during a visit to Media Prima Bhd (MPB).
The Diploma in English Communication students visited Balai Berita, MPB's headquarters, under Eduscape, an MPB initiative aimed at exposing students to television, radio, print and digital media operations.
[[nid:1525001]]
Led by News and Current Affairs (NCA) Production Support and Technical Operations manager Abdul Rahim Daim, the tour covered Media Prima Audio, NCA studios, Rev Media Group and the editorial floor of the New Straits Times, Berita Harian and Harian Metro.
The students also took turns anchoring the news at the studio, giving them a first-hand experience of what it is like to present a news programme.
Eighteen-year old Adam Iskandar Ardi Suhairi from Kuala Terengganu, said the visit opened his eyes to the work behind what audiences see and hear every day.
"I found the visit really fun. It was very interactive and interesting.
[[nid:1525000]]
"I never knew there was so much thought behind everything, from the radio station to the news anchors," he said.
Meanwhile, the hands-on experience also sparked interest in broadcast journalism among some students.
Nineteen-year old Adibah Raihanah Rahman, from Tawau, Sabah, said she was particularly drawn to news reading.
"I think I'm interested in journalism, especially news reading.
"It feels surreal. I got to sit on the news anchor chair and read the teleprompter by myself.
"I think that's such a beautiful experience, and I would like to experience it again," said Adibah.
Nurul Adawiyah Mohd Amli, 19, also shared a similar aspiration.
"I'm interested in becoming a newsreader because I think I have the talent for it," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia move closer to reopening Tebedu-Entikong trade route
Article:
JAKARTA: Malaysia and Indonesia are moving closer to reopening trade through the Tebedu-Entikong border route, with the remaining administrative matters expected to be resolved soon.
Indonesian Trade Minister Budi Santoso said both countries had agreed on the substantive and regulatory aspects of the border trade issue, with only a few administrative matters remaining.
"I don't think there are any issues concerning the border because we have agreed on the substantive and regulatory aspects. There may be some administrative matters that we still need to resolve, and hopefully these can be completed soon," he told Bernama.
He was met after co-chairing the fourth Malaysia-Indonesia Joint Trade and Investment Committee (JTIC) meeting here on Thursday with Malaysia's Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
Johari, who was interviewed alongside Budi, said Malaysia was ready on its side while Indonesia was working on the remaining matters.
"I think they are working on it because Indonesia also wants a lot of our products to go to them and they also want to export to us. So if the border is efficient, both parties will benefit," he said.
Tebedu, in Malaysia's eastern state of Sarawak, lies across the international border from Entikong in Indonesia's West Kalimantan province, forming a key land crossing between the two countries.
According to a Malaysian parliamentary reply, trade through Tebedu-Entikong declined after Indonesia imposed restrictions on seven categories of goods entering Kalimantan through the crossing from May 15, 2014, including food and beverages, clothing and textiles, footwear and electronics.
A Bernama report dated Sept 14 last year said Malaysia and Indonesia had agreed to reopen the Tebedu-Entikong route for bilateral trade following discussions between Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto in Jakarta.
The Entikong-Tebedu route was also among the key issues highlighted in the JTIC outcomes, with Budi saying during the joint press statement that both countries were committed to the effective implementation of the Border Trade Agreement (BTA) and continued efforts to facilitate border trade and strengthen economic connectivity through the crossing.
He said the meeting also addressed market access and trade facilitation, including agriculture and food products, stronger investment cooperation and a productive investment climate, as well as cooperation in areas such as e-commerce, agriculture, halal and standards.
Meanwhile, Johari said the fourth JTIC was the first meeting of the bilateral trade mechanism in nine years, adding that he had invited Budi to Kuala Lumpur for the fifth meeting next year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tanjung Lompat drowning: Second victim found, search continues for two
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: The second of four victims feared drowned at Pantai Tanjung Lompat, Bandar Penawar, here, was found by the search and rescue (SAR) team at 1.53pm today.
Tanjung Sedili Maritime Zone headquarters Operations Officer I Lieutenant Commander Mohamed Shafiee Bakar said the second victim was identified as 16-year-old Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor, whose identity was confirmed by his family.
"The victim was found floating at a location near where the first victim was found, about 800 metres away," he said at a press conference at the scene here today.
Shafiee said the second day of the SAR operation was still underway with the cooperation of various agencies, including the police, Fire and Rescue Department, as well as the local community and fishermen.
"We will maintain a search radius of two nautical miles for the two remaining victims.
"The challenge we are facing is waves reaching 1.5 metres in height," he said.
Yesterday, the first victim, identified as Alif Taqiuddin Kamal Hasrul, 16, was found at 1.25pm.
The two remaining victims yet to be found are Mohamad Haiman Fitri Supian and Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal, both 16.
Earlier, the media reported that four teenagers were feared drowned while two others were rescued after they went swimming at the beach about 8am yesterday.
The incident occurred when one of the victims nearly drowned, before his friends who tried to rescue him were also believed to have drowned.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia protesters targeted by coordinated disinformation
Article:
JAKARTA: Disinformation about recent anti-government protests in Indonesia has inundated social media in what researchers say is a coordinated attempt to spread propaganda about the one-year-old movement.
AFP fact-checkers have debunked dozens of posts about student-led demonstrations this summer on platforms such as Instagram and TikTok, including old footage of huge crowds and burning buildings shared alongside false claims that local media are ignoring widespread chaos.
Rallies last week in the capital Jakarta over worsening economic conditions and the government's handling of corruption did devolve into clashes with police, but the violence shown online was far worse than the reality on the ground – and activists say rumours are hurting their cause.
"Hoaxes can influence whether someone decides to join a protest or not," said Namora Siahaan, a member of the University of Indonesia Student Executive Board, a group behind similar rallies.
Namora cited the spread of false information about protest locations and student arrests, which he said are "likely intended to spread fear and discourage civilians from taking part in the demonstrations."
Police said they had detained hundreds of people in connection with last week's march on parliament, including 65 on suspicion of being "provocateurs."
Supriyono, another protest coordinator, told AFP he was concerned the unrest could have been deliberately provoked.
Last month authorities detained nine people and seized 10 social media accounts for allegedly spreading disinformation about possible riots, though they did not disclose who was behind it.
"The motives vary, including financial gain," said Iman Imanuddin, criminal investigation director for the Jakarta Metropolitan Police, during an Aug 7 press conference.
"Some suspects received orders or payment from other parties to produce and distribute the content," he added, about one week after calling the operation an "organised digital propaganda syndicate."
The campaigns come one year after protests over lavish perks for lawmakers spiralled into general anti-government anger – Indonesia's biggest unrest since President Prabowo Subianto took office in 2024.
[[nid:1524990]]
Multiple researchers have found evidence of a coordinated attempt to promote disinformation about more recent demonstrations, which have called in part for seizing corrupt officials' assets and ending the government's costly free school meals programme.
Ismail Fahmi, founder of data analytics company Media Kernels Indonesia, analysed about 29,000 social media posts between July and August and uncovered a campaign that amplified threats of looting and unrest, while downplaying protesters' demands.
The narratives contributed to a "perception in the public sphere that mainstream media have been co-opted by those in power and are deliberately censoring demonstrations," Ismail said – despite ongoing coverage from local and international news outlets.
Ika Idris, an associate professor at Monash University Indonesia, separately analysed nearly 35,000 posts on X in late July and found almost all of them came from accounts that "showed patterns that would have been almost impossible to carry out manually."
One video viewed more than 1.9 million times falsely presented aerial footage of a massive student protest in June as evidence that more large-scale rallies were going uncovered.
Similar posts debunked by AFP misrepresented a fire started by angry protesters in South Sulawesi province last year as a recent blaze at the parliament building.
Ika's analysis found one account reposted nine such claims within just over a tenth of a second – hinting at possible coordination.
She also saw a spike in rumours ahead of last week's anti-graft protest in Jakarta that the event had been cancelled.
"There was clearly an attempt to amplify it," Ika said.
While Ika could not determine who was behind the campaigns, some of the posts she analysed were "used by pro-government accounts to discredit those who criticise the government."
"The danger is multi-layered because this issue could delegitimise legitimate protesters," she said.
But the main victim, she said, is "not any particular political side, but rather the public's ability to distinguish what is real from what is not."
Bivitri Susanti, a member of the selection panel for the Shadow Cabinet, a watchdog group formed in July by academics and activists as a counterpart to Prabowo's administration, agreed that the spread of false information has created confusion about protesters' aims.
"Unfortunately, I feel that the efforts of those seeking to create such a situation have proven successful," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal flood toll hits 1,273 as 4,757 remain missing
Article:
KATHMANDU: Catastrophic floods on the China-Nepal border have killed at least 1,252 people in Nepal, the disaster authority said Thursday, taking overall deaths to more than 1,270.
Chinese state media earlier confirmed 21 people were killed in Tibet, bringing the total toll from  the disaster that struck on August 26 to 1,273.
The number of missing in Nepal remained 4,216, as rescue operations continued on a war-footing.
In China, state media say there are 541 people missing, taking the overall number to 4,757.
Nearly 600 foreigners from over 30 nationalities are also missing, with Indians making up one of the largest proportions.
Some 75 Americans are also unaccounted for, according to the State Department on Wednesday.
In Kathmandu, desperate families of some of the missing foreigners said they were combing hospitals and morgues for any information about their loved ones.
"I feel desperate, it's been so many days," said 53-year-old American Sanjeev Rai who flew to Nepal after learning that his wife was untraceable.
The floods, which tore through mountain districts, have destroyed roads, bridges and other infrastructure, hampering relief efforts.
Aid agencies said they were considering deploying porters to deliver aid to hard-hit districts close to the border with China.
"We've been discussing with the government how also to use helicopters, cargo drones to be able to deliver aid," Lila Pieters Yahia, the UN resident coordinator for Nepal, told reporters in Kathmandu.
"The beauty of your country (is) you have porters. So we have to go back into also those very simple means to bring the aid as soon as possible."
Long considered the backbone of trekking and mountaineering expeditions in Nepal, porters are known to carry heavy loads for days across steep trails in tough conditions.
Nepali army personnel and rescue teams, including foreign experts, meanwhile continued to search Thursday for survivors feared trapped inside several hydropower tunnels.
The work is ongoing using excavators and other heavy equipment to look for any survivors in the tunnels, the army said.--AFP

Title: How quickly can Canada pivot?
Article:
THE resignation of a Prime Minister, one leadership race, a general election, and 23 months later, Canada is now back where it first started: with the Canadian Prime Minister having to reluctantly announce a 'dollar-for-dollar' tariff against its southern neighbour: United States.
But things are different this time around. When Prime Minister Justin Trudeau announced a dollar-for-dollar retaliation in January 2025, he stood alone.
Opposition Leader Pierre Poilievre was scathing in his response, and Canadians feared that the backlash from the US would be the end of the special relationship of the two North American neighbours.
Fast forward to August 2026 and the vibe in Canada is very much different. When Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the same, starting Sept 8, nearly all Canadian provincial governors expressed support for it.
The Canadian public cheered him on, even as the projected economic impact of the double tariffs seemed to paint a less than rosy future for Canada.
Something about Mark Carney just seems to 'sit right' with the Canadian public.
His approval ratings are among the highest for any Canadian Prime Minister, at 56 per cent while Poilievre's stands at a dismal 18.4 per cent. This is a far cry from January 2025 when Poilievre was leading Trudeau by 25 percentage points as the preferred Prime Minister for Canada.
Carney, with his solid and perhaps somewhat staid background in banking and finance, does not come across as a natural wordsmith.
Yet his speeches now are packed with memorable quotes, from "they asked too much, and offered too little" (referring to the US offer during the trade negotiations), to his rallying cry of "Canada has what the world wants" and to the very subtle yet sarcastic "we recognise that sometimes its signature was written in pencil" (referring to how the US kept breaking its word).
For a country that exports 77 per cent of its products to the United States, the fallout from the tariffs are expected to be staggering.
Canada accounts for only 12 per cent of the total international trade of the US, but yet there are some sectors that are so closely intertwined that both countries will feel the impact of the tariffs.
The 50 per cent tariff on aluminum from Canada, for example, just simply does not make economic sense, given that Canada supplies more than half of the aluminum that is needed by the US.
Interestingly enough, the US has steered clear of imposing tariffs on other 'important' items: Canadian crude which makes up 63 per cent of all US oil imports, and Canadian potash which makes up nearly 90 per cent of the total US potash imports.
[[nid:1524983]]
Ontario Governor Doug Ford has threatened to cut off the electricity that his province supplies to 1.5 million American homes. But the reality is that if Ontario were to stop exporting electricity, the United States would be able to cover the shortfall.
It would be a bit more expensive, but the northern states of the USA would not be "plunged into darkness".
Now that the US tariffs on Canadian products have been put into place, the estimates on the Canadian economy are startling, to say the least.
One economist from the University of Calgary predicts that at least 90,000 Canadian jobs will be lost, and unemployment could rise to seven per cent by the end of the year. Already, Canadians are bracing for a difficult winter when summer was already not in their favour.
Food Banks Canada, which helps more than two million Canadians put food on the table, has in the past year raised the alarm over the increasing number of children who rely on food banks – with almost one-third of food bank dependents under the age of 18.
In response, the Canadian Government has put in place the Canada Groceries and Essential Benefits, essentially to subsidise the grocery bills of 12 million low and middle-income Canadians - nearly one-third of Canada's total population.
Canadians have banked on the strength of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) to cushion the tariffs, since most of the goods traded are CUSMA-compliant, meaning that it avoids being tariffed.
Yet even that is now in jeopardy. In July of this year, Trump signalled that he was not interested in renewing CUSMA, meaning that it would automatically expire in 2036, unless extended.
The 10-year period gives Canada some breathing space. That is, unless the US decides to invoke Article 34.6 and unilaterally withdraw from CUSMA, in which case the United States would only need to give six months' notice to both Mexico and Canada.
Mark Carney was spot-on when he warned that defending Canada's sovereignty in the face of the US tariffs "will hurt before it gets better".
The question now is whether Canada can diversify fast enough.
* The writer is a foreign service officer who has served in bilateral and multilateral posts
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mersing passenger boat detained, crew held for overloading
Article:
MERSING: A passenger boat carrying 18 people, six over its permitted capacity of 12, was detained by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) off Pulau Besar yesterday.
The vessel's 22-year-old skipper and 35-year-old crew member were also detained.
The vessel was intercepted about 1pm, some 0.4 nautical miles northwest of the island, during a routine patrol.
Mersing MMEA Maritime Zone deputy operations director Lieutenant Maritime Hazuan Joha said initial checks found the vessel was also operating with insufficient crew.
"Checks found the passenger boat was carrying passengers beyond its permitted capacity and operating without the required number of crew," he said in a statement today.
The skipper, crew member and vessel were escorted to the Mersing Maritime Zone headquarters jetty before being handed over to the agency's investigating officer.
The case is being investigated under the Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1952 and Boats Rules 1953.
Those found guilty could face a fine of up to RM10,000 for each offence, depending on the applicable provisions.
Hazuan reminded passenger and tourist boat operators to comply with licensing conditions, safety regulations and maritime laws to ensure passenger safety.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China sends third batch of aid to Nepal after flood disaster
Article:
BEIJING: China has sent a third batch of aid to Nepal after the Aug 26 flooding disaster, including tents, blankets, medical protective suits and satellite communication equipment, the foreign ministry said on Thursday.
The China Meteorological Administration and Nepalese meteorological authority have been in contact for video weather consultation and real-time information sharing, and the Tibet region has also provided emergency assistance, the ministry said.--REUTERS PIC

Title: Oriental Kopi's FMCG gross margin strongest in four quarters – HLIB Research
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd's gross margin for the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) segment in the third quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26) was the strongest in four quarters, said Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB Research).
The FMCG segment's gross margin of 44.7 per cent was 8.6 percentage points higher than in the preceding quarter, the research firm noted, and comfortably ahead of the approximately 42 per cent average between the fourth quarter of FY25 and second quarter of FY26.
"With a 44.7 per cent gross margin versus 21.5 per cent for café chains, FMCG growth should be structurally margin-accretive at the group level," said HLIB Research in a Sept 3 note, maintaining its outlook with a 'Buy' call and RM1.17 target price.
The FMCG business' gross margin was driven by its external business – the selling and distribution of ready to consume food and beverage products through external channels – with revenue being up 66.1 per cent year-on-year.
HLIB Research expects the external FMCG business' long-term trajectory is supported by its collaborations with FamilyMart and Inside Scoop, distribution opportunities alongside the Indonesian joint venture, and the planned canned ready-to-drink coffee, which is expected to be launched by later this year.
Nevertheless, Oriental Kopi is facing slower same-store sales growth (SSSG) in the nine-month period ended June 30, 2026 (9M FY26), which is attributed to some major disruptions at some of its top-performing outlets, such as City Square Johor Baru, Kuala Lumpur International Airport, Pavilion KL and KLCC, with the latter three affected by decline in tourist arrivals arising from the Iran War.
SSSG in 9MFY26 grew by 0.5 per cent across its 15 outlets, compared with a growth of 12.6 per cent in the corresponding period in FY2025, across 11 outlets.
Having said that, HLIB Research said that it does not expect a clear SSSG recovery for Oriental Kopi in the coming quarter, and see Q1 FY27 as the more meaningful read on the mature base.
This is because while the tourist-heavy outlets should be able to recover from Q4 FY26, City Square JB will not reopen until October, which implies that sales growth there would only have a lift from Q1 FY27 onwards.
Despite the weaker SSSG, Oriental Kopi's revenue grew 34.2 per cent year-on-year in Q3 FY26, mainly driven by new outlet openings.
On overseas expansion, Oriental Kopi's Indonesian joint venture with Erajaya is targeting its first outlet at Central Park Mall, West Jakarta, by end-2026, while its Mauritius franchise is expected to open its first outlet within five to six months.
HLIB expects both ventures to have a limited impact on FY26 and FY27 earnings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Family forced to stay in fire-damaged home after Merdeka blaze
Article:
PASIR GUDANG: A family's Merdeka celebration turned into a nightmare when they were alerted that their rented home was on fire — just 200 metres from where they were celebrating.
Hazwani Zainordin, 39, her husband and their three-year-old son were attending a Merdeka programme at a community hall near their flat in Taman Desa Rakyat Perdana on Aug 23 when they heard cries of "Fire! Fire!"
"Everything was fine when we left home. About an hour later, we were told our house was on fire.
"We rushed back and found the kitchen badly damaged, while almost the entire ceiling was blackened by smoke," she said when met.
Hazwani said neighbours managed to contain the fire before firefighters arrived and later helped clean up the family's home.
The fire, believed to have been caused by a short circuit, destroyed electrical appliances and furniture.
The family has continued living in the damaged house as they have nowhere else to go and cannot afford higher rental costs.
Hazwani's husband works as a factory operator, while the family also cares for their three-year-old son, who has heart, hearing and right-hand abnormalities.
The boy requires regular medical check-ups at the National Heart Institute and Sultanah Aminah Hospital, as well as treatment at two other hospitals, including one in Melaka.
"We have put off repainting the smoke-blackened walls until we can afford it. We also have other important commitments to deal with," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tanker safely refloats after running aground near Sungai Johor Bridge
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: The tanker that drifted and ran aground near the Sungai Johor Bridge yesterday has safely refloated and moved to its designated anchorage.
Senai-Desaru Expressway Berhad (SDE) said technical inspections found that the bridge structure remained safe and the incident had not affected road users.
The concessionaire said the tanker, SMF IXORA, reportedly
drifted towards the bridge
at about 2.30pm while sailing towards its anchorage amid strong currents and winds.
"The bridge remained open to traffic as normal, with the vessel towed clear of the bridge and moved to its designated anchorage at 3.16pm yesterday," it said in a statement.
Meanwhile, the Johor Port Authority (LPJ) said the vessel was towed clear of the bridge.
LPJ said it was working with relevant agencies to monitor the situation and ensure navigational safety in the area.
"LPJ is conducting further investigations to determine the actual cause of the incident and assess any impact or damage that may have occurred," it said in a statement today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's foreign worker intake based on industry needs, says Ramanan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has dismissed claims that it plans to recruit 200,000 Bangladeshi workers over the next six months.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said foreign labour intake would be determined by verified industry needs and the ceiling set under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP).
He said the figure cited by a Bangladeshi junior minister did not reflect Malaysia's current needs and described the proposed recruitment timeline as illogical.
"How does it make sense for 200,000 workers to come within six months? Does that mean more than 1,000 Bangladeshi nationals will have to enter Malaysia every day?
"It's not logical at all," he said when contacted.
Ramanan said foreign worker recruitment would be considered on a sector-by-sector basis and only where there was a genuine need.
He said such requests would be assessed within the ceiling set by the Economy Ministry under the 13MP before being brought to the cabinet for consideration.
"Only when there is a genuine need will the matter be assessed and discussed by the cabinet," he said.
Ramanan said the approach was intended to ensure decisions on foreign labour intake were made in a measured and responsible manner, based on actual economic and industry requirements.
He added that the federal government would continue to consider the needs of employers and critical sectors while prioritising job opportunities for Malaysians and ensuring reliance on foreign workers remained within the approved policy framework.
Ramanan was responding to reports quoting Bangladeshi Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Junior Minister
Mir Shahe Alam
as saying Malaysia would recruit about 200,000 Bangladeshi workers in stages over six months, beginning at the end of this month.
Yesterday, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil had said that the junior minister's statement should
not be regarded
as an official declaration by the Bangladeshi government.
He said Ramanan had informed him that the claim did not represent Malaysia's position.

Title: 19 Thai undocumented migrants deported
Article:
BUKIT KAYU HITAM: Malaysia deported 19 Thai illegal immigrants through the Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security Complex here.
The Kedah Immigration Department said the group comprised 14 men and five women who had previously been detained at the Belantik Immigration Depot in Sik.
They were deported yesterday after completing sentences for offences under the Immigration Act 1959/63 (Act 155) and Immigration Regulations 1963.
"As part of continued enforcement, all the illegal immigrants were also blacklisted in the immigration system to prevent any attempt to re-enter Malaysia in the future," the department said.
"The deportation programme is part of continued enforcement by the Kedah Immigration Department to curb the presence and activities of illegal immigrants in the country," it said.
The department said it would continue to intensify enforcement, detection, arrests, prosecution and deportation of illegal immigrants to safeguard national security, public order and sovereignty.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas-Umno unity must not be seasonal - Afnan Hamimi
Article:
KOTA BARU: The unity between Pas and Umno must not be seasonal, appearing only when an election is near and disappearing once it is over, said Pas Youth chief Afnan Hamimi Taib Azamudden.
He said both parties needed to build a relationship that transcended political interests and election seasons.
"We cannot only unite when we want to win, and return to bickering after securing victory.
"Nor can we only come together when we have a common enemy, but go our separate ways when political interests change," he said in his keynote address at the Pas Youth Wing muktamar today.
Afnan said unity did not mean eliminating other groups, adding that efforts to strengthen the Malay-Muslim community should not come at the expense of the rights of other races and religions.
"Pas and Umno youth are also working together, serving as a bridge towards greater unity among the ummah.
"We may come from different parties and political histories, but when the greater interests of the ummah are at stake, we must seek common ground that unites us.
"The seed has already been planted. We have seen how the relationship and synergy began to take shape in Johor and developed to the point where we can enjoy its fruits in Negri Sembilan.
"A seed will not grow on its own, just as a tree will not flourish without being nurtured. Likewise, relations among Muslims must be nurtured," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Akmal maintains stance to sit out Melaka polls if BN, PH cooperate
Article:
KOTA BARU: Datuk Dr Muhammad Akmal Saleh has maintained his stance that he will not contest as a candidate if Barisan Nasional decides to cooperate with Pakatan Harapan in the upcoming Melaka election.
The Umno Youth chief said he would not compromise his principles for the sake of a position.
"My stance, from then, now and forever, is that I will not cooperate with PH. If BN and PH cooperate, I myself will not contest as a candidate.
"For me, when we fight for something, we must have principles. I will not compromise my principles for the sake of a position.
"My stance is not merely that of a state assemblyman, but also that of the Umno Youth chief," he said during a press conference here today.
He said he had previously called for Umno to leave the government and become the opposition, but the party had decided to remain in the unity government until the end of the current parliamentary term.
Following the decision, he said he would maintain his stance of not contesting in the  Melaka polls if BN and PH decided to cooperate.
"It is not that I do not want to be a candidate, but at the Umno Youth Special Convention early last year, we had already expressed our desire for Umno to leave the government.
"That was our firm stance.
"After the convention, the party decided to remain in the government until the end of the current parliamentary term.
"We respect that decision, but this time, my stance is that I will not contest if BN and PH cooperate in Melaka. That remains my stance, then, now and forever," he said.
Earlier, Dr Akmal attended the Pas Youth Congress here with 25 other BN representatives comprising Umno Youth leaders from the central and state levels.
Dr Akmal described his attendance at the Pas Youth Congress as a show of support for the Pas Youth Council in its efforts to promote Muslim unity.
"I think we all know that our agenda is to unite the ummah. In fact, the theme of Pas Youth Malaysia is 'Leading Unity', which is actually almost similar to that of Umno Youth," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nearly 90pct of Tabung Haji RCI recommendations near completion
Article:
BANGI: Nearly 90 per cent of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) recommendations to improve Lembaga Tabung Haji's (TH) internal governance are expected to be completed following amendments to the relevant Act and the institution's regulatory framework.
TH chairman Tan Sri Rashid Hussin said most recommendations under the institution's jurisdiction had already been implemented, with the remaining matters requiring cooperation from the government and relevant agencies.
"Most recommendations under the institution's internal jurisdiction have already been implemented.
"The remaining matters involve external processes that require cooperation from the government and relevant agencies.
"One of the key lessons from the RCI report is that what happened to TH in the past must not be repeated, particularly in terms of corporate governance and integrity," he said during the Dialog Ummah: Realiti dan Masa Depan TH today.
Rashid said TH could not rely solely on trust in people but must strengthen its checks and balances to ensure the institution remained resilient, well-governed and free from interference that could undermine depositors' confidence.
He said TH had implemented various improvements in corporate governance, liquidity and risk management as part of efforts to fulfil the RCI recommendations.
The institution had also engaged experts to enhance its training and governance programmes, while strengthening its board committees and giving their chairmen greater powers to ensure more comprehensive oversight.
Rashid said the final step was to ensure external factors affecting TH were regulated by the relevant institutions.
"It takes time, but we have reached the final stage and, God willing, TH will be regulated by the relevant institution," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Families descend on Nepal in search of missing tourists
Article:
KATHMANDU: Desperate families of missing foreigners were clinging to hope as they combed hospitals and morgues in search of clues, a week after catastrophic floods tore through Nepal's Himalayan border region.
Outside Kathmandu's tourist police headquarters, Sanjeev Rai was trapped in agonising uncertainty.
The 53-year-old American flew to Nepal after learning that his wife, Jiwan Jyoti, was untraceable while returning from a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, the sacred peak revered by Hindus and Buddhists.
"The day I arrived, I said, let's find a helicopter; I'm going to look for her," Rai told AFP.
But Timure, the village in Rasuwa district where she was when disaster struck, remains inaccessible and dangerous.
"I feel desperate; it's been so many days," he said.
Jyoti, an engineer at Intel, had embarked on the journey as a spiritual quest and an adventure to mark her 50th birthday.
Now Rai says he has all but abandoned hope of finding her alive.
"I'm no longer counting on survivors. I just hope the DNA samples will match. I want to be able to mourn."
The August 26 flood has become one of the deadliest disasters to hit the Himalayan nation in recent years.
The huge wave of debris has killed more than 1,200 people and left more than 4,750 missing in Nepal and China's Tibet region, smashing towns, roads, bridges and multiple hydropower dams.
According to Nepali police, some 294 foreigners have been rescued, most of them Chinese and Indian nationals.
But 583 foreigners remain unaccounted for, many of them pilgrims who had spent months preparing for the demanding trek around Mount Kailash.
Rob Fenn, Britain's ambassador to Nepal, said the embassy was doing its best to provide verified information to its nationals searching for their loved ones.
"I think the nature of this disaster is an agonising long wait for closure and information," he told AFP.
"We have reinforced the embassy... with psychosocial experts. We've set up a reception centre for families."
Among the missing are also 77 pilgrims from spiritual leader Sadhguru's Isha Foundation, including Europeans, North Americans and Australians.
Several of their relatives have travelled to Kathmandu seeking answers, assisted by volunteers from the foundation.
"We go to the Nepali police every day to get information on those who have been rescued. We examine photos... published by the police," said volunteer Arun Mehta.
Others spend their days visiting hospitals.
But all the members of the group, including three Nepali guides, remain missing till now, Mehta said.
"They had completed their pilgrimage around Mount Kailash and were going through immigration procedures" at the Gyirong border crossing with China when disaster struck, he said.
The foundation has provided identifying details to authorities, including distinctive snake-shaped rings and pendants worn by many pilgrims.
Nepal police began collecting DNA samples from relatives this week to build a database for identifying bodies, while families overseas will be able to submit samples in their home countries.
Thousands of kilometres away in Russia's far east, some relatives are making plans to join the search in Nepal.
From Yakutsk, the brother of missing musician Kirill Tretiakov, said he would travel to Nepal within days.
"For the moment, we have no information about Kirill," he told AFP. "We hope his group survived but ended up without any means of communication."
Tretiakov was travelling with a group of Russian and Ukrainian pilgrims organised by the travel agency Tashi Delek.
"We will start our search with the hospitals. No matter how long it takes, we will keep looking for him."
Another trek organiser, Fishtail, says it has lost contact with a group of 20 pilgrims, mostly Malaysians, who were travelling with guides and drivers.
"No one could escape; it was so sudden," said Nimsang Gurung, a sales representative with the company.
As search efforts continue, officials fear the disaster will have a big impact on tourism, a major source of revenue for the country.
"The tourism sector is going to suffer from this disaster," said Sunil Sharma of Nepal's National Tourism Agency, even though "only four districts" were directly affected.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kedah RTD seizes lorry with road tax, insurance expired since 1997
Article:
JERLUN: The Kedah Road Transport Department has seized a lorry found operating with a road tax that expired in 1997 and without valid insurance coverage.
Kedah RTD director Stien Van Lutam said the lorry, which was carrying rice husks, was stopped during an enforcement operation in the Jerlun area.
He said the 29-year-old driver was also found to be operating without a valid Goods Driving Licence (GDL).
The driver reportedly worked only as a delivery driver, transporting rice husks to destinations specified by the lorry owner.
"The lorry had been driven to various locations despite having no valid road tax or insurance coverage for 29 years. This could endanger other road users, particularly if an accident occurs.
"Checks also found that its inspection certificate from the Computerised Vehicle Inspection Centre (Puspakom) had expired.
"The seizure was carried out to ensure vehicles that do not meet the required eligibility and documentation standards are not allowed to continue operating on public roads," he said.
He also reminded commercial vehicle operators and drivers to ensure their motor vehicle licences, insurance, Puspakom inspections and vocational licences remain valid before operating their vehicles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ministry ready to offer psychosocial support to families of Malaysians affected by Nepal disaster
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry is ready to provide psychosocial support and assistance to the families of Malaysians affected by the disaster in Nepal if required.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri, said the ministry is currently awaiting updates from the Foreign Ministry before coordinating any assistance.
She said her ministry cannot act independently and must work alongside the Foreign Ministry to determine the specific needs of the affected families.
"We must go through the Foreign Ministry. We were informed that if they require assistance, they will notify us.
"We will work together through the Foreign Ministry. We cannot simply intervene on our own," she told reporters after attending the 80th Anniversary Celebration of the Social Welfare Department at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre today.
Nancy added that among the support services the ministry can offer are counselling and welfare assistance to help affected families cope with the situation.
Yesterday, the cabinet was informed by the Foreign Ministry that 77 Malaysians who were found safe in Tibet and Nepal following devastating floods in the region last week were being brought to Kathmandu for repatriation to Malaysia.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the cabinet was also informed by Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan that another 55 citizens remained unaccounted for.
He noted that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had approved a US$1 million contribution to support humanitarian efforts in the region.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bank Negara maintained OPR on resilient global growth, contained domestic inflation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia has maintained the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent at its fifth Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting of 2026, leaving the benchmark rate unchanged for the year so far.
The central bank said the monetary policy stance is consistent with the outlook of continued price stability and sustainable economic growth.
However, the MPC will remain vigilant to ongoing developments and assess the balance of risks surrounding the outlook for domestic inflation and growth.
"The latest indicators point to resilient global growth, supported by strong global tech expansion, improving supply conditions and stable labour markets.
"Inflation has edged lower in recent months but is expected to remain elevated given the lagged pass-through of energy costs to consumer prices.
"Going forward, while uncertainties surrounding the Middle East conflict will continue to weigh on global growth amid continued inflationary pressures, the impact is expected to be cushioned by sustained tech-related spending," the central bank said in a statement.
Bank Negara last adjusted the OPR in July 2025, when it cut the rate by 25 basis points from three per cent to 2.75 per cent as a pre-emptive measure to cushion economic growth against external headwinds.
The Malaysian economy expanded 5.7 per cent in the first half of 2026, driven by stronger-than-expected export performance and sustained domestic demand.
Bank Negara expects the solid momentum to bring full-year growth to around five per cent, with sound economic fundamentals expected to support resilient growth in 2027.
The central bank said growth will be supported by robust demand for electrical and electronics (E&E) goods, stronger technology-related non-E&E exports and sustained tourist spending, while stable labour market conditions and ongoing investment activity are expected to underpin domestic demand.
However, Bank Negara said the outlook remained subject to risks from a prolonged Middle East conflict and lower commodity production.
Stronger global growth, firmer technology-related export demand and higher tourism activity could provide upside to the outlook.
On inflation, headline and core inflation averaged 1.8 per cent and two per cent respectively in the first seven months of 2026.
Bank Negara said the pass-through of elevated costs to consumer prices had remained contained by domestic policy measures, stable demand and limited spillover from the stronger external sector to wages.
"Developments surrounding the Middle East conflict remain uncertain, as elevated global commodity prices continue to exert upward pressure on cost conditions.
"As these developments remain fluid, the MPC will remain vigilant to cost pressures and domestic demand conditions given their impact on the inflation outlook," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Senior Citizens Bill expected in Parliament early 2027, says Nancy
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Senior Citizens Bill, previously targeted for tabling at the October Dewan Rakyat session, is now expected to be brought to Parliament early next year.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the draft bill is complete, but the process has taken longer due to new elements raised during engagement sessions with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and state governments.
She said the ministry initially aimed to table the bill this year, but additional amendments required further review.
"Our timeline was indeed for this year, but during our engagement sessions, many new points were raised to be included.
"We agreed to incorporate them as amendments to our draft. Since we engaged with NGOs, including at the state level, this has extended the timeline," she said.
She met reporters after attending the 80th Anniversary Celebration of the Social Welfare Department at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre today.
The event was officiated by the prime minister's wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
Also present was Media Prima TV Networks group editor for news and current affairs Datuk Azhari Muhiddin.
Nancy added that the drafting process still requires careful examination before the bill can be finalised and brought to the next stage.
Earlier in her speech, Nancy expressed her appreciation to all department personnel for their constant readiness to assist people affected by disasters and for being among the first responders during emergencies.
She said the dedication of department staff in going down to the ground, managing temporary relief centres, assisting victims, and providing emotional support to affected groups earned them the title "Orange Jacket Heroes".
She added that the moniker is not merely about the colour of their uniform, but symbolises their willingness to step out of their comfort zone to safeguard the welfare of disaster victims.
"For example, when a fire disaster occurs in Sabah, among the first mentioned is the Social Welfare Department.
"We are always ready with information to respond and ensure immediate action is taken," she said.
According to Nancy, this experience reflects the government's responsiveness in ensuring proper measures are taken for every disaster-related development.
She said the department's achievements to date were not the effort of a single generation, but a legacy built and carried forward from one generation to the next.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia primed for economic leapfrog, best chance since 1997: Liew
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has its best opportunity since 1997 to leapfrog economically as the post-pandemic shift from efficiency to resilience reshapes global business and investment, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said.
He said Malaysia must seize the opportunity by tackling existing challenges, developing solutions and turning them into investable opportunities.
"Malaysia is now having the best opportunity since 1997 to leapfrog and we must seize the opportunity while dealing with the challenges that confront us, and maybe turn challenges into solutions, and crucially, investable opportunities.
"The shift from a global 'efficiency' model to a 'resilience' model post-pandemic presents strategic opportunities for Malaysia," he said in his keynote address at the Malaysia Private Capital Forum 2026 here today.
Liew said the economy grew six per cent in the second quarter of 2026, bringing first-half growth to 5.7 per cent and demonstrating resilience amid global volatility.
He said key growth drivers included Malaysia's participation in the global artificial intelligence boom, particularly in semiconductors and data centres, as well as the palm oil, oil and gas, tourism and services sectors.
Liew highlighted several key challenges and investment opportunities for Malaysia.
He said Malaysia must transform from a trading nation into a technology nation by strengthening its role across the semiconductor ecosystem, including outsourced semiconductor assembly and testing, advanced packaging, integrated circuit design and equipment.
He noted that the country holds a strategic "indispensable middle" position in the global tech and tax landscape, especially as geopolitical tensions increasingly divide the world.
Liew also identified urban revitalisation as a key investment opportunity, calling for a shift away from urban sprawl towards rebuilding inner cities, repurposing vacant buildings and creating mixed-use urban spaces.
He said decentralising financial expertise beyond Kuala Lumpur could also unlock regional investment opportunities, particularly in Penang and Kulim for technology and semiconductors, Sarawak for energy, and Johor for cross-border supply chains.
Liew said Malaysia was also well-positioned to lead Asean's growth by leveraging its Islamic finance infrastructure and private capital networks to drive regional deals and investments.
He also highlighted demographic changes as both a challenge and an investment opportunity.
Liew said Malaysia's relatively young population, with a median age of 31, remained an important source of future economic growth, while an ageing society was also emerging.
He cited changes in local manufacturing trends, noting that a factory that mainly supplies Malaysia and regional neighbours was producing fewer baby diapers and more adult diapers.
He said this presented both challenges and opportunities in healthcare, elderly care and public-private investment in services for the elderly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt mulls permanent Law Reform Commission
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is studying a proposal to establish a permanent Law Reform Commission to review national laws and recommend reforms in a systematic, continuous and evidence-based manner.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the proposed commission would serve as a permanent, specialised and structured mechanism to study the country's laws and recommend reforms independently and based on evidence.
Azalina said law reform should not be carried out on an ad hoc basis or only when a crisis emerged, but should be undertaken in a planned manner to ensure the country's legal framework remained relevant and responsive to society's needs.
"The proposal to establish a Law Reform Commission as a permanent, specialised and structured mechanism to study national laws and put forward reform recommendations systematically, continuously, independently and based on evidence.
"Law reform should not be ad hoc or only driven when a crisis arises, but should be carried out in a planned manner so that the country's legal framework remains relevant and responsive to the current needs of society," she said.
Azalina was speaking at the launching ceremony of the Public Opinion Survey on the Drafting of the Coroner Bill at the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC).
Also present were BHEUU director-general Datuk Zamri Misman and deputy director-general (Law Reform) Datuk Thiyagu Ganesan.
Azalina said the proposal formed part of the government's broader institutional reform agenda aimed at strengthening the country's legal framework.
She said a permanent mechanism would allow law reform to be undertaken systematically rather than only in response to specific cases or crises.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Philippines stages school safety drill after shootings
Article:
BULACAN: As an alarm warning of an active shooter threat blared through a Philippine public school on Thursday, students and teachers moved swiftly into action.
Some students helped lock and stack chairs against classroom doors, while others drew curtains, switched off lights, and crouched under desks as teachers instructed them to stay quiet and out of sight.
The scene at Carlos F. Gonzales High School in Bulacan province was part of a nationwide school safety drill led by the Philippines' Department of Education and its security agencies, as authorities seek to strengthen emergency preparedness following two recent school shooting incidents.
Under a scripted active-attack scenario, which did not use active-shooter role players, school officials alerted emergency responders, activated a warning system and placed classrooms under lockdown while students sheltered in place until police declared the campus secure.
[[nid:1524904]]
"Our topmost priority is safety and preparedness," school principal Ceanceno Espirito Jr. said, adding that the drills allow schools to assess emergency response measures and identify areas for improvement.
The drill rehearsed a full emergency response, including coordination with police, evacuation to designated assembly areas, headcounts of students and staff, first-aid treatment for simulated casualties and psychosocial support for those affected.
School shootings are rare in the Philippines, where firearms are tightly regulated. But recent incidents have prompted renewed debate about gun ownership, firearm storage, and children's exposure to social media.
A shooting at a high school in the southern Philippines on Aug 18 left two students dead, including the alleged gunman.
It was the second school gun attack in the Philippines in less than three months and happened days after a high-profile incident in Thailand, where a student went on a shooting rampage at a school on the outskirts of the capital Bangkok.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Every reportable death deserves same level of scrutiny, says Azalina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Every death that requires reporting should receive the same level of proper scrutiny, regardless of whether it attracts national attention, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
She said this was among the principles underpinning the proposed Coroner Bill, which aims to establish a clearer, more independent and transparent framework for investigating deaths and strengthen families' right to know what happened to their loved ones.
"Justice cannot depend on whether a case goes viral. Every death that must be reported should receive the same and appropriate level of scrutiny, whether it receives the attention of the whole country or is mourned only by a family," she said.
Azalina was speaking at the launch of the Public Opinion Survey on the Drafting of the Coroner Bill at the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) here today.
Azalina said Malaysia already had a framework for inquests under the Criminal Procedure Code, particularly Sections 328 to 341A, as well as Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019.
However, she said death investigations had become increasingly complex, involving digital evidence, forensic analysis, medical records, institutional security and coordination among multiple agencies.
She said the government was therefore examining the need for a dedicated Coroner Act to provide a clearer and more comprehensive legal framework.
Azalina said the proposed legislation would have three main objectives: establishing a clear and comprehensive legal framework; creating a more structured, independent and transparent coronial system; and clarifying the responsibilities of each party when a death was reported.
She said the system should not only determine the cause of death but also identify weaknesses that could help prevent similar tragedies from recurring.
"If a death exposes weaknesses in a system, the coroner's findings should not end up in a file because the lessons learned from a case should help us protect other lives," she said.
Azalina said the study would examine several aspects, including categories of deaths that must be reported, the jurisdiction and independence of coroners, standardised procedures, inter-agency coordination, preservation of evidence, timelines for action and the rights of families throughout the process.
She stressed, however, that the policy parameters for the proposed Bill had yet to be finalised.
Azalina said she hoped the Bill could be tabled in Parliament this year, but acknowledged that next year might be more realistic because Parliament would have its Budget sitting in October.
"I have asked if it is possible to be done this year. But we have the Budget sitting in October. Perhaps next year would be better," she said.
She said the proposed reform should not be viewed as an attack on any institution or profession, but as an effort to clarify responsibilities, reduce overlaps and strengthen public confidence in institutions.
"Death does not know political colour, and a family's grief has no ideology," she said.
Azalina said the proposed Coroner Bill was ultimately aimed at ensuring families received a fair and credible process when a death raised questions.
"The law may not be able to promise every family the answers they want to hear or hope for.
"But the country must guarantee something fundamental — their right to a process that is independent, detailed, humane and thorough," she said.
Azalina said the government would consider the views gathered through the public opinion survey in developing a framework that was not only sound on paper but fair, practical and effective.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FMM pushes for 3pct GST return
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturing (FMM) has renewed its call for the return of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) at an introductory rate of 3.0 per cent, arguing that a lower consumption tax would ease the burden on businesses while strengthening Malaysia's industrial competitiveness.
FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said the previous 6.0 per cent rate had placed a significant burden on businesses and consumers, making a lower 3.0 per cent rate a more reasonable starting point.
"We felt that a reasonable rate of three per cent would be more acceptable to the market. With the reduced GST burden of three per cent, I think the industry would have more capacity to undertake more productive manufacturing activities," Lee said at a press conference, here on Thursday.
The proposal forms part of FMM's wishlist for the 2027 Budgey and includes safeguards for essential consumption, simplified compliance for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and reliable refund mechanisms.
FMM said a lower-rate GST could help cost pressures and competitiveness challenges faced by manufacturers under the current Sales and Services Tax (SST) system.
Citing FMM's first-half 2026 Business Conditions Survey on the impact of the current SST system, he said 60 per cent of manufacturers reported higher production costs from embedded supply chain taxes, while 59 per cent cited unrecoverable taxes on business inputs.
Some 45 per cent of manufacturers faced compliance and administrative burdens, while 42 per cent reported uncertainty over the scope, exemptions and interpretation of the SST. Another 34 per cent reported higher output costs, 32 per cent cited reduced price competitiveness, and 22 per cent faced cash flow pressures.
"SST is adding to manufacturers' costs through embedded and unrecoverable taxes, while administrative complexity and uncertainty compound the burden. The findings highlight the need to address tax cascading and simplify compliance to protect competitiveness and cash flow," Lee said.
Following the government's indication that it is open to studying selected GST features within the SST, FMM also recommended systematic input tax credits or offsets.
It said effective relief for essential goods and exports, along with prompt refunds, would help reduce tax cascading, embedded production costs and cash flow pressures.
Beyond tax reform, FMM called for the 2027 Budget to focus on expanding Malaysia's productive capacity by enabling businesses, particularly SMEs, to retain and reinvest more capital in technology, innovation, talent development and domestic supply chains.
Its recommendations are structured around four priorities, which include competitive industries, domestic industrial development, a highly skilled workforce, and energy transition and circular economy adoption.
Under its competitiveness agenda, FMM proposed an RM1.5 billion smart manufacturing support package for 2027 to 2030, comprising RM500 million for automation, RM750 million for manufacturing digitalisation and RM250 million for artificial intelligence adoption.
It also proposed an RM1 billion manufacturing research and innovation endowment fund, jointly funded by the government and industry, alongside more accessible research and development incentives.
To strengthen domestic industrial capabilities, FMM called for an RM100 million national supply chain resilience fund to help manufacturers secure critical inputs, qualify alternative suppliers and diversify supply sources.
It also proposed expanding export incentives and market development support, updating the SME manufacturing definition to companies with annual turnover of up to RM100 million and/or up to 300 employees.
On talent development, FMM proposed channelling 60 per cent of foreign-worker levy proceeds into skills development and 40 per cent into automation, supported by RM100 million and RM500 million in seed funding, respectively.
It also called for greater industry-led technical and vocational education and training, teaching factories and apprenticeships, including a 50 per cent apprenticeship wage subsidy capped at RM1,000 a month for 12 months.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three NGO chairmen fined RM600 each for using unauthorised symbols
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Three non-governmental organisation (NGO) chairmen were fined RM600 each after being convicted of using their organisations' symbols without approval from the Registrar.
The three were charged at the magistrate's court yesterday under subsection 50(3) of the Societies Act 1966.
The provision carries a maximum jail term of three months or a fine of up to RM3,000 upon conviction.
Magistrate Aini Adilah Muhammad Faizal imposed a RM600 fine on each accused, or one month in jail if they failed to pay.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Lim Zhan Yi led the prosecution.
According to a statement by the Registrar of Societies (RoS), the prosecution followed an inspection and enforcement operation conducted by the Putrajaya and Penang RoS, in cooperation with enforcement officers from the Penang Home Ministry office, on Aug 27.
"We want to remind all registered organisations that the use of any emblem, symbol, sign, signboard or clothing associated with an organisation must obtain approval from the Registrar, as required under the Societies Act 1966.
"We will continue monitoring registered organisations and take enforcement action to ensure compliance with prevailing laws," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Search continues for two more after second teen confirmed drowned in Kota Tinggi
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 3 — The body of one of the three teenagers who went missing while bathing at Tanjung Lompat Beach, Kota Tinggi was found at 1.53 pm today.
Tanjung Sedili Zone Maritime headquarters operations officer Lieutenant Commander Mohamed Shafiee Bakar said Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor, 16, was found floating about 800 metres from the location where the first victim, Alif Taqiuddin Kamal Hasrul, was found yesterday.
He said the victim’s body was safely brought to the shore at around 2.50 pm this afternoon and was confirmed dead by health officials.
“The family has also been identified and confirmed that the body is that of the victim who went missing yesterday,” he said at a press conference at the scene of the incident, here today.
He said the victim’s body has been taken for a post-mortem at the Kota Tinggi Hospital.
He said the search for Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal and Mohamad Haiman Fitri Supian, both 16 years old, was ongoing, with a search radius of seven nautical miles from the northwest of the beach.
“The search with the other agencies will continue until the victim is found,” he said.
Yesterday, Kota Tinggi deputy district police chief DSP Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad was reported to have said that the body of the first victim, Alif Taqiuddin, was found about 500 metres from the location where he was reported missing.
Fire and Rescue Service Department announced that it received an emergency call at 8.19 am regarding the incident, with six 16-year-old victims being part of a group of 15 people who had come to camp in the area for the past two days.
However, two of them were successfully rescued by the public, while the other four were missing and feared drowned. — Bernama

Title: Law minister: Coroners Bill to be tabled next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — The Coroners Bill, aimed at clarifying the management of death cases, is expected to be tabled in Parliament next year, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
She said the bill was originally targeted for tabling this year, but with the Budget 2027 session in October, it is more suitable to bring it next year.
Azalina said drafting the law is expected to establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) and detail the roles of coroners and relevant parties in handling death cases.
“We hope that with this act, we can establish SOPs and answer questions that arise. We do not want families searching for answers when a death occurs,” she told reporters after launching the Public Opinion Survey on the Drafting of the Coroners Bill here today.
Azalina said, although procedures for death investigations exist under current legislation, the Coroners Act will complement them and offer clearer guidance on implementation.
Earlier in her speech, Azalina said specific legislation on coroners is being considered with three main goals: establishing a clear and comprehensive legal framework; creating a more structured, independent and transparent coroner system; and clarifying each party’s responsibilities when a death is reported.
“We also want a system that not only determines the cause of death but also identifies weaknesses to prevent similar tragedies from recurring.
“If a death reveals weaknesses in the system, the coroner’s findings should not end up buried in a file because the lessons learned from a case should help us protect other lives,” she said.
Azalina added that Malaysia currently has an inquest implementation framework under the Criminal Procedure Code, specifically Sections 328 to 341A, as well as Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019.
However, she said that death investigations have become more complex, involving digital evidence, forensic analysis, medical records, institutional safety, and inter-agency coordination.
Azalina said that the ongoing inquest proceedings into the death of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir serve as a reminder of the importance of evidence management, post-mortems, inter-agency coordination, and early communication with families.
She also cited the cases of the late Muhammad Adib Mohd Kassim and the late Teoh Beng Hock, as well as custodial deaths such as those of the late A. Kugan and the late S. Balamurugan, as reminders of the need for an independent, thorough, and credible process when serious questions arise surrounding a death.
She said the need for this legal reform had also been raised by the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (SUHAKAM), the Malaysian Bar, the Tun Dzaiddin Royal Commission Report, and the Royal Commission of Inquiry into the death of Teoh Beng Hock.
“The principle is simple: justice should not depend on whether a case goes viral. Every death that must be reported deserves the same scrutiny, whether it catches nationwide attention or is mourned by a single family,” she said.
Meanwhile, Azalina said the government is examining a proposal to establish a Law Reform Commission as a permanent, dedicated, and structured mechanism to review national laws and systematically submit reform recommendations on an ongoing, independent, and evidence-based basis.
She stressed that law reform need not be ad hoc or driven solely by crises but should be executed in a planned way to ensure the national legal framework remains relevant and responsive to current social needs. — Bernama

Title: Azalina: PM term limit and AG/PP separation Bills ready for Parliament
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — A Bill to limit the tenure of the prime minister is ready for its second reading in the Dewan Rakyat, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
However, she said the decision on whether to table the Bill at the next parliamentary sitting rested with the Leader of the House, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“Everything is ready. The limit on the prime minister’s term is ready. It is subject to the Leader of the House, the Prime Minister, on whether we want to bring it for a vote at the next sitting,” she told reporters after launching the Public Opinion Survey on the Drafting of the Coroners Bill here today.
Azalina said the proposed term limit for the prime minister would involve amendments to the Federal Constitution and would therefore require the support of a two-thirds majority in Parliament.
She said the same applied to the Bill on the separation of the roles of the Attorney General (AG) and Public Prosecutor (PP), which would also require a two-thirds majority.
“Since both Bills involve amendments to the Federal Constitution, we need a two-thirds majority. The same applies to the separation of the roles of the AG and PP, which also requires a two-thirds majority. So, domestic politics does play a role,” she said.
In this regard, Azalina appealed to all members of parliament, regardless of political affiliation, to support the proposed reforms, saying they could help reduce perceptions of politically motivated prosecutions.
“I sincerely hope that members of the Dewan Rakyat, the Dewan Negara and all political parties will welcome these Bills because they bring more benefits than drawbacks. This is for our country,” she said.
